docs.title: Home
docs.text:
This is the homepage for HandyUI documentation.

You will get introduced to HandyUI and the reason to it's existence here.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Code-only (like WinForms)
  • Uses SkiaSharp for rendering
  • Open Source and free to modify

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
Basically, I (davpnuser) was trying to make a modern, hardware-accelerated GUI app in C# and modern .NET. I tried using WinForms, Uses GDI+. What about WPF? Uses XAML. Well, what about Avalonia? Nope, it has a lot of boilerplate. WinUI Markup? Sucks.

So, i was basically trying to find a option that didnt exist so at one point i got tired and started using SkiaSharp with WinForms. (yes, i know, i was using the exact framework i didnt use at first.) And it was going good until... I realized that WinForms is NOT cross-platform. So, i decided to try using alternatives such as OpenTK's C# library and Silk.NET and etc.

But, ultimately, i found that Silk.NET works best. So, i was then using pure Silk.NET and SkiaSharp for a while until i realized once again, that, there was a lot of boilerplate. So, i began work on HandyUI. At first, it was really incapable. Really. Incapable. Then, over time, it started getting better with more and more updates.

My decision of seperating the core renderer to a seperate library especially helped me out when i wanted to make a Silk.NET adapter. I first made the Silk.NET adapter, and once it got stable enough, i deprecated the WinForms (legacy) adapter.

docs.title: What's next for HandyUI?
docs.text: I can't tell. It has way more features than it used to have, but still, im a solo developer. Don't expect much advanced work from me. I'm a human too, after all. Still, i will be maintaining this package as long as i physically can until i either get burnt out or i take a break. But, you should not expect advanced built-in controls from me. That is your work. You can use a control library; Make a control library. Do what you want but dont expect advanced controls from me.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The public API of HandyUI is split across three packages:

  • HandyUI.Core - renderer, controls base class, modules, helpers, theming, animation.
  • HandyUI.Controls - a set of ready-to-use controls built on HandyUI.Core.
  • HandyUI.SilkNet - a windowing adapter that hosts a UIRenderer inside a GLFW-backed window.

docs.title: BaseControl
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Base.BaseControl

The base class for every drawable control. Provides transformation, geometry, visual state, interaction state, and a parent/children tree.

public abstract class BaseControl : IControl

Nullable mouse position

DoesIntersect and OnUpdate receive SKPoint?. null means "the cursor is not over this subtree" (clipped out). Custom controls should treat null as not hovered.

docs.title: Location / Bounds
docs.text:
public SKPoint Location { get; set; }
public SKRect  Bounds   { get; set; }

Location is the offset from the parent (applied only when ParentChildPositioningEnabled is true). Bounds is the rectangle in this control's local space.

docs.text:

Higher = drawn later (on top) and hit-tested first. Children are sorted lazily; InvalidateChildrenOrder() is rarely needed.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public sealed class ClickBox : BaseControl<ClickBox>
{
    public event Action? Clicked;

    public override bool DoesIntersect(SKPoint? p)
        => p is { } value && Bounds.Contains(value);

    public override void OnUpdate(float dt, SKPoint? mouse) { }

    public override void OnDraw(SKCanvas canvas)
    {
        using var paint = new SKPaint
        {
            Color = IsHovered ? SKColors.Orange : SKColors.CornflowerBlue
        };
        canvas.DrawRect(Bounds, paint);
    }

    protected override bool OnMouse(MouseEventContext ctx)
    {
        if (ctx.Type == MouseEventType.Click)
        {
            Clicked?.Invoke();
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}

new ClickBox().WithBounds(0, 0, 160, 48).WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

HandyUI.Core.Enums.BorderDirection

Specifies where a stroke is drawn relative to the shape it outlines.

public enum BorderDirection
{
    Inside,

docs.title: MouseEventContext
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Data.MouseEventContext

public record MouseEventContext(
    SKPoint? ClientPosition,
    MouseEventType Type,
    MouseButton Button = MouseButton.None,
    int WheelDelta = 0);
Field Description ClientPosition Cursor position in the receiving control's local space, or null when clipped out of this subtree. Type Event kind (Move, MouseDown, MouseUp, Click, Wheel). Button Which mouse button triggered the event. WheelDelta Wheel delta in "clicks" (±120 per notch).

Null means clipped

ClientPosition is null - not a sentinel - when the control is outside its parent's clip region. Treat null as "not hovered" and return false from DoesIntersect.

docs.title: HandyWindow
docs.text:
HandyUI.SilkNet.Components.HandyWindow

A Silk.NET/GLFW-backed window that runs its own pump thread, marshals calls with Invoke, integrates with ThemeHelper for OS appearance, and applies Win32 tweaks when available.

public class HandyWindow : IDisposable

Windows only

The Silk.NET adapter currently supports Windows only. Construction throws PlatformNotSupportedException elsewhere.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
public HandyWindow(WindowConfiguration windowConfiguration);

Creates the underlying window on a dedicated thread and returns once the window handle exists (not necessarily initialized).

The constructor also:

  • calls ThemeHelper.EnsureInitialized(), which reads the OS accent + light/dark mode and pushes them into ThemeManager;
  • registers the window with ThemeHelper for automatic re-invalidation on OS theme changes.
var window = new HandyWindow(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Demo" });

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
Attach a renderer, add controls to it, and run:

var (window, renderer) =
    WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default);

renderer.AddRootControl(
    new Button().WithText("Save").WithLocation(20, 20));

window.Run();

Add controls to the renderer, not OnLoad

UIRenderer.AddRootControl is thread-safe and queues the control for the next tick. There is no reason to wait for the GL context - only operations that genuinely need a live context (like the window icon) are deferred automatically.

docs.title: ResourceManager
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Components.ResourceManager

Loads resources from disk or from embedded assembly resources.

public static class ResourceManager

Lookup order

For a path like Assets/logo.png, the manager tries:

  1. AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory/Assets/logo.png on disk.
  2. The entry assembly, the executing assembly (HandyUI.Core), and any registered assemblies - matching a manifest resource whose name ends with Assets.logo.png.

First hit wins.

docs.text:
public static Action<string, string>? WhenErrored { get; set; }

Optional callback invoked when a lookup fails and ignoreErrors was false. Receives (detail, path). If null, the manager throws FileNotFoundException.

ResourceManager.WhenErrored = (detail, path) =>
    Console.Error.WriteLine($"Couldn't load '{path}': {detail}");

docs.text:

docs.title: GetResourceByPath(...)
docs.text:
public static bool GetResourceByPath(
    string relativePath,
    out Stream? resourceStream,
    bool ignoreErrors = true,
    IEnumerable<Assembly>? additionalAssemblies = null);
Parameter Description relativePath Assets/icon.png or a manifest resource name. resourceStream On success, a seekable MemoryStream at position 0. ignoreErrors If false, failures go through WhenErrored (or throw). additionalAssemblies Extra assemblies checked in addition to the global registry. 
if (ResourceManager.GetResourceByPath("Assets/logo.png", out var stream))
{
    using var data = SKData.Create(stream!);
    using var image = SKImage.FromEncodedData(data);
}

Stream is a snapshot

Embedded resources are copied into a MemoryStream before being returned - safe to hand to SkiaSharp regardless of the source.

docs.title: ThemeHelper
docs.text:
HandyUI.SilkNet.Helper.ThemeHelper

Detects the operating system's accent color and light/dark mode, feeds them into ThemeManager, and re-invalidates all open windows when the OS theme changes.

public static class ThemeHelper
{
    public static event Action<Appearance> AppearanceChanged;

    public static void EnsureInitialized();
    public static void Deinitialize();

    public static void RegisterWindow(HandyWindow window);
    public static void UnregisterWindow(HandyWindow window);

}

Windows and Linux

  • Windows 10+: reads HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM\AccentColor and AppsUseLightTheme, and watches SystemEvents.UserPreferenceChanged.
  • Linux: reads org.freedesktop.appearance over the XDG portal D-Bus (accent-color and color-scheme), and subscribes to SettingChanged.
  • Other platforms: returns FallbackColor / ThemeMode.Unknown.

Bundles the two OS values.

docs.title: AppearanceChanged
docs.text:
public static event Action<Appearance> AppearanceChanged;

Raised whenever the OS accent or light/dark mode changes. Subscribing automatically starts the watcher; unsubscribing the last handler stops it.

docs.title: EnsureInitialized()
docs.text:
public static void EnsureInitialized();

Idempotent. Reads the current appearance, subscribes ThemeManager to AppearanceChanged, and starts the OS watcher. HandyWindow's constructor calls this for you - you only need to call it explicitly if you're using HandyUI.Core without the Silk.NET adapter.

public static void RegisterWindow(HandyWindow window);
public static void UnregisterWindow(HandyWindow window);

var appearance = ThemeHelper.GetAppearance();
Console.WriteLine($"Accent: {appearance.AccentColor}, Mode: {appearance.Theme}");

Apply once at startup

If you're not using the Silk.NET adapter, apply the OS theme manually:

var a = ThemeHelper.GetAppearance();
ThemeManager.Instance.SetTheme(a.AccentColor.Red, a.AccentColor.Green, a.AccentColor.Blue, a.Theme);

docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Theming.ThemeManager

A process-wide singleton that generates a full color system from a single base color (usually the OS accent) and a light/dark mode, using OKLCH tonal mapping. Every built-in control reads its colors from here at draw time, so changing the theme updates all controls live.

public sealed class ThemeManager
{
    public static ThemeManager Instance { get; }

    public ThemeMode Mode { get; }
    public event Action? ThemeChanged;

    public void SetTheme(byte r, byte g, byte b, ThemeMode mode);

    public SKColor GetTone(int tone);

    // Derived properties …
}

ThemeManager vs Theme

ThemeManager is live - it holds a base color + mode and generates tones on demand. Theme is a static palette. Built-in controls use ThemeManager by default; Theme is available when you want to freeze a specific palette per-control.

docs.title: Instance
docs.text:
public static ThemeManager Instance { get; }

The one and only instance. Thread-safe to access.

docs.text:
public ThemeMode Mode { get; }

The current light/dark mode. Read-only; set via SetTheme.

docs.title: ThemeChanged
docs.text:
public event Action? ThemeChanged;

docs.text:
public void SetTheme(byte r, byte g, byte b, ThemeMode mode);

Replaces the base color and mode. Clears the tone and derived caches, then raises ThemeChanged.

ThemeManager.Instance.SetTheme(0x25, 0x63, 0xEB, ThemeMode.Light);

You usually don't call this

The recommended path is ThemeHelper.EnsureInitialized(), which reads the OS appearance and calls SetTheme for you. Call SetTheme directly only when you want a custom accent independent of the OS.

docs.text:
public SKColor GetTone(int tone);   // tone in [0, 900]

Generates (and caches) a color from the current base at the given OKLCH tone. 0 is nearly white, 900 is nearly black; 500 is the accent. Internally calls ColorEngine.GetToneRgb.

var accent = ThemeManager.Instance.GetTone(500);
var surface = ThemeManager.Instance.GetTone(100);

SurfacePrimary 0 800 Card / input surface. SurfaceSecondary 50 700 Alternate surface. SurfaceTertiary 100 600 Alternate surface, deeper. TextPrimary 900 50 Main text. TextSecondary 800 100 Secondary text. TextTertiary 750 150 Hint / placeholder text. Accent 500 500 Brand / interactive. AccentHover 600 400 Hovered accent. Border 200 700 Strokes and separators. Property Description TextDisabled TextPrimary at 72 % transparency. Shadow Black at 80 % (light) / 62 % (dark) transparency.

docs.title: ColorEngine
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Theming.ColorEngine

Static OKLCH-based tone generator used internally by ThemeManager.

public static class ColorEngine
{
    public static (byte R, byte G, byte B)
        GetToneRgb(float baseR, float baseG, float baseB, int requestedTone);
}
Parameter Range Meaning baseR/G/B 0-255 Source color (usually the accent). requestedTone 0-900 Tone. 0 ≈ white, 900 ≈ black, 500 = accent.

GetToneRgb converts the base to OKLCH, keeps its hue, maps lightness to the requested tone, and reduces chroma near the extremes so pure white/black anchors look clean.

You rarely call this

ThemeManager.GetTone already caches results. Use ColorEngine only if you need a tone from a different base color than the current theme.

docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Data.Theme

A plain palette record with public SKColor fields. Every built-in control exposes a Theme property you can swap to customize its colors.

public record Theme
{
    public SKColor PrimaryColor          = SKColor.Parse("#2563EB");
    public SKColor SecondaryColor        = SKColor.Parse("#3B82F6");
    public SKColor DisabledColor         = SKColor.Parse("#E2E8F0");
    public SKColor TextColor             = SKColor.Parse("#0F172A");
    public SKColor LightTextColor        = SKColor.Parse("#FFFFFF");
    public SKColor DisabledTextColor     = SKColor.Parse("#94A3B8");
    public SKColor BackgroundColor       = SKColor.Parse("#F8FAFC");
    public SKColor DarkerBackgroundColor = SKColor.Parse("#FFFFFF");
    public SKColor ActiveColor           = SKColor.Parse("#2563EB");
    public SKColor SemiActiveColor       = SKColor.Parse("#DBEAFE");
    public SKColor BorderColor           = SKColor.Parse("#CBD5E1");

    public static Theme Default => new();
}

Fields, not properties

Theme uses public fields rather than auto-properties. You can mutate a Theme instance in place (theme.PrimaryColor = SKColors.Red;) and use with expressions - the record's compiler-generated copy constructor copies fields, so both styles work.

Theme vs. ThemeManager

Theme is a static palette you attach to a control. The live, system-aware palette is ThemeManager, which generates colors dynamically from the OS accent color. Theme does not react to ThemeManager.ThemeChanged.

docs.text:

docs.text: Field Default Typical use PrimaryColor #2563EB Accent / brand. SecondaryColor #3B82F6 Less-emphasized accent. DisabledColor #E2E8F0 Fill for disabled controls. TextColor #0F172A Primary text. LightTextColor #FFFFFF Text on dark / colored backgrounds. DisabledTextColor #94A3B8 Text on disabled controls. BackgroundColor #F8FAFC Panel / control background. DarkerBackgroundColor #FFFFFF Window background (default canvas clear). ActiveColor #2563EB Highlight for the active / selected item. SemiActiveColor #DBEAFE Hover / soft highlight. docs.title: Building custom palettes
docs.text:
var dark = Theme.Default with
{
    PrimaryColor          = SKColor.Parse("#F97316"),
    BackgroundColor       = SKColor.Parse("#131E37"),
    DarkerBackgroundColor = SKColor.Parse("#090C13"),
    TextColor             = SKColor.Parse("#F8FAFC"),
    BorderColor           = SKColor.Parse("#3F719A")
};

new Frame()
    .WithTheme(dark)
    .WithSize(320, 180)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

Theme.Default allocates a new record on every call, and Theme.Default == Theme.Default is false (reference equality on record instances compares fields, so Equals works - just don't use ReferenceEquals).

A frame-driven float interpolator built on BaseModule<Tweener>. Every UIRenderer owns one and registers it as a module, so tweens run automatically while the render loop ticks.

docs.title: Current
docs.text:
[field: ThreadStatic]
public static Tweener? Current { get; private set; }

The tweener active on the current thread. UIRenderer sets this to its own Tweener before dispatching input, updating modules, and rendering - so inside a control's OnUpdate/OnDraw/OnMouse you can just do Tweener.Current.To(...) without wiring anything up.

if (Tweener.Current is { } tweener)
{
    tweener.To(0f, 1f, 0.2f, v => _hover = v, EaseType.SineOut);

docs.text:
public TweenHandle To(
    float start, float end, float duration,
    Action<float> onUpdate,
    EaseType ease = EaseType.Linear,
    Action? onComplete = null);

Starts a tween from start to end over duration seconds. Returns a TweenHandle for controlling it.

var handle = tweener.To(0f, 1f, 0.3f,
    v => _progress = v,
    EaseType.CubicOut,
    () => Console.WriteLine("done"));

The tween is queued and applied on the next OnUpdate. It runs once by default; use the handle's Reverse() to run it backwards.

docs.title: TweenHandle
docs.text:
HandyUI.Core.Data.TweenHandle

A lightweight struct wrapping an internal tween job.

public readonly struct TweenHandle
{
    public bool IsValid { get; }

    public void Pause();
    public void Play();
    public void Cancel();
    public void Reverse();
}
Member Effect IsValid false once completed or cancelled. Pause() Freezes progress at the current value. Play() Resumes a paused tween. Cancel() Stops the tween and resets its value to the start (or end when reversed). Reverse() Runs the tween backwards from its current position.

Cancel behaviour

Cancel() invokes onUpdate once more with the reset value so your visual state snaps back to a sensible place.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
public sealed class Fader : BaseControl<Fader>
{
    private float _opacity;
    private TweenHandle _tween;

    protected override bool OnMouse(MouseEventContext ctx)
    {
        if (ctx.Type == MouseEventType.Click && IsHovered && Tweener.Current is { } t)
        {
            _tween.Cancel();
            _tween = t.To(_opacity, 0f, 0.3f, v => { _opacity = v; Invalidate(); });
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    public override bool DoesIntersect(SKPoint? p) => p is { } v && Bounds.Contains(v);
    public override void OnUpdate(float dt, SKPoint? mouse) { }
    public override void OnDraw(SKCanvas canvas) { /* use _opacity */ }
}

docs.title: Common conventions
docs.text:
• Autosizing - every control runs ResizeToContent() in its constructor and whenever relevant properties change. Leave Width and Height at their defaults (usually 0) to auto-size to content.
  • Theming - controls read colors from ThemeManager at draw time, so changing the OS theme updates every control live. Controls that also expose a Theme property use it for per-control overrides.
  • Events - callback events follow the WhenXxx naming convention (WhenClicked, WhenToggled, WhenTextChanged, …). Fluent helpers attach to them directly (OnClicked(...), OnToggled(...)).
  • Animations - hover, ripple, focus, and checkmark animations use Tweener. They degrade gracefully if no tweener is available (values snap to target).
  • Disposal - every control disposes its internal SKPaint and SKTypeface instances in OnDispose.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
A quick heads-up

All code examples in this page use the C# 9 feature Top-level Statements.

Getting started with HandyUI also includes creating a testing window.

You have two options:

  • Create one window

    or

  • Create multiple windows

Creating a single windowCreating multiple windows

docs.title: You can create a window just like this:
docs.text:
using HandyUI.Controls.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Data;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Helper;

var (window, renderer) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default);

new Label()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithFontSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

await window.RunAsync();

Here's the result of running the piece of code given above:

docs.title: You can also create multiple windows at the same time.
docs.text:
using HandyUI.Controls.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Data;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Helper;

var (window1, renderer1) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Window 1" });
var (window2, renderer2) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Window 2" });

new Label()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithFontSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer1);

new Label()
    .WithText("Hello World, Once Again!")
    .WithFontSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer2);

await Task.WhenAll(window1.RunAsync(), window2.RunAsync());

Here's the result of running the piece of code given above:

docs.title: Creating a window with a custom configuration
docs.text:
You can do this by passing in a configuration object with parameters into the window creation function.

The example i will give right here is changing the title of the window.

To do this, you can create a WindowConfiguration object with the Title property set to the title you want.

using HandyUI.Controls.Controls;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Data;
using HandyUI.SilkNet.Helper;

var configuration = WindowConfiguration.Default with { Title = "Your title comes here!" };

var (window, renderer) = WindowHelper.CreateWindowAndGetRenderer(configuration);

new Label()
    .WithText("Hello, World!")
    .WithFontSize(24)
    .WithLocation(15, 15)
    .WithAddToRenderer(renderer);

await window.RunAsync();

Here's the result of this example:

For more info on custom configurations, you can check out the WindowConfiguration page in the API Reference.
